EDIT 3 (The 1.3 Update): To be clear upfront, the 1.3 update is a fantastic step in the right direction. Hard Mode is now more sensible and less of a highroll crapshoot, the changes to how memory cards work is fantastic, and the option to tone down flashing lights is very appreciated.

However.

I still cannot recommend this game. While the changes are great, they're missing one critical fix. Earning Rainbow Holographic (and therefore Lord of the Pit) still [i]requires[/i] Hard Mode, rather than making it an option. This demonstrates that the devs still don't see the issue with the change they made and how it's disrespectful towards players. I just can't get behind a dev team that's willing to throw out the progress [i]they[/i] asked of the player, especially considering there's nothing to say they won't move goalposts again, whether for LotP or something else. I've seen some argument that the change was made because the original 'win three times' condition wasn't engaging/was too repetitive, but even if that's the reason they changed it, that doesn't even fix the issue seeing as hard mode only requires one less win, and the increased difficulty means you're going to be making just as many if not more attempts to earn it. I've said it before and I'll say it again: if they wanted to make LotP connected to Hard Mode, they should've made it an [b]alternative[/b], not a replacement.

Dev encourages players to find synergies between items to tip the scales of luck in their favor. When streamers find synergies that let them bend the game over their knee, (which is really fun and what they were told to do,) the dev proceeds to nerf every powerful item without stating any other reason than over powered sorry as to why. This game went from feeling like a difficult but fun gambling game to something that felt like you were actively being crippled in every run if you were able to get past deadline one.

I enjoyed my time with the game for a while, got every ending, but it gets pretty stale. The memory cards are potentially a great incentive to keep you playing, as they offer various modifiers that can completely alter how you play.

However, the only way to unlock memory cards is to go into a new deadline with enough money to already complete it. Which is extremely RNG dependent of you having an amazing run early. There's also no way to unlock specific cards, it's yet-again more RNG. So if there's one you really want, you're stuck grinding and crossing your fingers over and over again.

But the worst part? The cards are single use. You can select a memory card, lose on the first deadline through no fault of your own because the slot machine refused to give you enough money, and now that memory card is unusable. Gone forever, until you get lucky enough to find it again.

Outside of that, the RNG is just very annoying at times. As stated before, losing on the very first deadline is more common than you'd expect. Unlike Balatro, where you can choose what hand you play and can plan around which cards still remain in your deck, the odds of discarding and drawing what you need for a certain play, understanding what hands will give you enough chips to clear the blind and move on. CloverPit is literally just pushing a button. No interaction, not much planning. You can tweak the odds, give yourself more rolls, synergize trinkets so they alter the odds even more. Feels good at first, but the more I unlocked the more the items in the shop feel useless, won my first 3 runs in ~1.5hr since then haven't gotten past 2nd deadline. Unlocking stuff feels like a de-buff and overall the gameplay leaves you lacking any sense of agency.

Pretty good game, very unique gameloop, theming, and visual style, but its 90% luck 10% skill. Yes I know "its gambling" Yes Yes I know. *I know*. But Balatro is literally poker and does something more transformative and skill based with its concept than Cloverpit does. With the dlc out now after no real gameplay tweak updates (we got a hard mode before real balancing), Im motivated to actually write a review on this game that could have been great. 
 
Early Game: 
With the game being a demonic slot machine you'd think the game is to "beat" the house and overcome the luck factor of the game. But in practice, It is entirely too difficult to genuinely get a run going when the shop offers you absolutely nothing.  Either charms that are impossibly expensive for the first 2 rounds or things that do not help the early game. For example, what do you do when your first three rerolls are filled with interest items, 666 items, scalable items, and extremely situational items? Round one and the best thing you can buy only benefits one symbol? Tough luck! This is especially bad when doing runs with corpse parts due to higher quotas. Comparing this to several other roguelikes, there isnt an earlygame as hellish as Cloverpit's (even balatro gold stake runs give me more agency in whether I win or lose).  
 
Late Game/Endgame: 
While the early game is a tedious grind until you get a good shop roll, the late game (within meta context) is frustrating as well. To get an ending, you need 5 cadave

Here's every run following the initial novelty:
1.Invest the time to get corpse parts and skull for a single run (buy 4 charms, shelf them, restart run and pray you hit the skull charm). They're required for the 'real' ending. The corpse parts each increase the total winnings required to hit the next deadline. Also there's no way to skip dialogue or animations so get used to seeing this.

2. Lose the run because you can't reach the increased debt.  You need to invest the time to get the corpse parts again.
2a. Win first deadline -> Get 0 charms that will contribute beneficially to your current or next deadline. You lose, invest more time setting up.
2b.Win first deadline -> Answer phone. Try to pick something that synergizes with your charms, but almost nothing will impact you this early. Get a charm that might help your current run. Check the requirements. 
2b1. Requirements: Achieve something after <X> spins in a row without a reward. Result: You'll hit 3 cherries after getting nothing for the previous spins due to how "luck" works. This immediately disables the charm and you lose ~3 spins to achieve ♥♥♥♥-all. You lose, invest more time setting up.
2b2. Requirements: Keep red button charged with other charms and use the button abilities. Result: 8/10 times you won't get anything to recharge the button, button abilities aren't strong enough to beat 2nd, 3rd, or 4th deadline. You lose, see you in 2 more runs.

I genuinely loved CloverPit up until the 1.2 update. I’ve put a good amount of time into the game and was steadily working toward 100% completion. I was totally happy to keep grinding, until this patch essentially punished anyone who hadn’t already finished the hardest achievements.

The biggest issue is the new requirement for upgrading memory cards to holographic. Previously, you unlocked holographic versions by winning with that card three times. Now you must beat that card in the newly-added Hard Mode, where your debt is doubled. This change sounds fine in theory, but in practice it makes several memory cards borderline impossible to clear. Some cards already alter the game so heavily that just winning once is difficult, doubling the debt on those cards turns them into instant “throwaways.” And unfortunately, you need every card holographic to unlock a certain achievment.

Players who already earned the achievement before 1.2? They’re done. Players like me, who were one card away? We’re now facing challenges that are mathematically close to unwinnable. The last card I needed was Delusions of Granduer, which doubles your debt. I was one win away from turning it holographic. Now, to make it holographic, I have to beat that card with the debt doubled again. You can’t even get out of the first round on Hard Mode with some of these setups.

On top of that, the charm “rebalancing” is almost entirely a series of nerfs. The patch describes these changes as making things “fairer,”

Honestly, at first the game is super fun (even after it isn't "fun" it still is tbh). Proves that the concept of gambling is fun even when you aren't gaining anything from winning IRL. The problem is that the whole goal is to increase your chances of winning by using lucky charms that you purchase with tickets you earn while you play. You basically combine perks to try to create an ideal slot machine that consistently pays you out. Some charms are ♥♥♥♥♥♥ stupid, some are really helpful and compound the value of symbols and patterns or give you a "luck" bonus every here and there, or lower the chances of seeing symbols you don't want to see. What sucks is that you don't choose what charms will be available for purchase (6 per round), and you have to pay more and more as the game progresses to re-roll the charms that you can buy, which is still basically just another slot machine, but a way more expensive and disappointing one usually.

Additionally, as you play, you unlock more lucky charms, which seems cool at first, but then you realize 99% of the ones you're unlocking will make you lose, so every time you unlock a charm it has a chance of appearing in the store, decreasing the chances of getting the good ones and making your chances of winning go down. It's a fun concept but it would be much more fun if you could choose your favorite charms to increase the chances of them appearing in the store. With the update, endless runs were patched out, and the high deadlines get harder even faster than they already did. The worst part is that you now only get holographic cards in Hard mode. Before, three normal runs were enough. With the Golden Calf card you already start with double the normal debt, and now in Hard mode you suddenly have four times the debt. You’d basically need two jackpots in each of the first three rounds just to survive – completely impossible. Really bad patch…

DO NOT BUY THIS GAME EXPECTING TO 100% IT

Early on, while getting unlocks and getting memory cards, this game is actually pretty good. It was a fun and simple rougelite that was hard, and took a bit to get the train rolling to understand and get better at this game. And that's what makes some of the best rougelites out there, simple to play but difficult to master, with lots of fun unlocks helping greatly.

But these devs want to cater to about 5 or 6 youtubers than are known for breaking games and making infinite money. As such, they are nerfing every other item to the ground. For a single player game, this is absurd, but normally these patches didn't dramatically affect games, you could still master this. This only affected maybe 5% of people playing to the extremes.

Until their recent 1.2 patch. The only challenge left for me was memory cards, which each one had a unique and fresh experience making players rethink entire strategies. Now, with the change to rainbow cards, say goodbye to that achievement. Expect to reset a run 10+ times just to get lucky enough for the FIRST deadline. Because resetting a game for RNG is what makes a game fun.

Thank you Panik Arcade for catering to a couple Youtube slop videos, which by the way is what made your game popular in the first place. As a congratulations for selling 1 MILLION copies, ruin the experience for everyone else.

after the latest update i can no longer recommend this game as they nerffed a lot of things and removed endless mode in a game that was all ready kinda tedious to even get a good run. instead of improving the game and adding QoL or actual content they are more focused on taking the fun out of the game, i will probably be uninstalling it as i wasnt having much fun before the update and now i just see no point in playing as the developers are ruining it further.

Seems like every time I play the game, it becomes less fun. I don't know if that's on patch changes or item unlocks, probably both. I remember the game felt kind of whimsical to play when it first came out, and I'm sad that it lost that.
devs already asking for paid dlc on a unfinished game that really lacks depth ...

While I don't regret my purchase of CloverPit overall given the cost of it, I think that this game lacks the actual interaction and significant choices that a game like, say, Balatro offer. The amount of significant choices are tiny compared to the amount of "action forward" clicks (pulling the lever, in particular). 

Obviously this isn't as bad as something like Snakes & Ladders, where there are zero meaningful choices, but most of the time, it's not a matter of choices that determine your win or loss, but rather random chance on what Lucky Charms are available for your purchase, and when. "Pulling" the lever is a meaningless mechanic; it could be streamlined by having a menu option that auto-spins all currently-remaining spins, rather than having to click every single time to pull the lever. 

Again, at the price point of $8 USD, it was cheap enough to be worth experiencing... but not really worth replaying to try to beat. You'll have to decide whether that makes it worth buying yourself.

its good for some time, but dont expect another good really amazing and replayable roguelike

the addition of hard mode just does the same old "who cares, they want hard mode ill give them double the requirements and thats it", its really low effort and REALLY frustrating on some memory cards

I love the concept and atmosphere. If you have a good run, it's very satisfying. 
 
But the game gets too repetitive and I feel like it doesn't offer many viable strategies. In the end you either restart runs until you get a few good items out of the decently large item pool to survive the first rounds or you just hope to be lucky (which you most likely won't). 
 
It was fun for a few hours, but that was it. Maybe get it on a sale, if you're curious.

the first and maybe second playthroughs are great, once you unlock more items it goes downhill very quickly, the RNG store is not fun. You are dependent on getting 'good luck' for the first couple of deadlines, you do not have the funds to refresh the store and your performance in the first and second deadlines dictates how many tickets you have to buy items. It is very difficult to get through the early game because so many of the items are made to slowly scale, before they are unlocked the item pool seems much better tuned for early game. There is one item that gives you increased luck for the final spin, there are 7(iirc) items that increase the multiplier for each individual symbol in the machine (under some conditions), 1:7 on the thing I want? insane. Likely made by a real gambler.

The creator decided to have unskippable cinematic sequences that end up feeling like the bulk of gameplay, the ticket dispenser, dispensing a ticket (every round), the slot machine dispensing coins (every round), the floor shaking (every round) it's just lazy.

If you think this is "Balatro but slots" you must be truly awful at Balatro. A better comparison would be "Luck Be a Landlord unnecessarily in 3D" but try to work in something about it not being very fun.

I don't normally write reviews like this, so I'll cut the fat and just say that if you have no intention of being a completionist about this game, I would completely recommend it. Fun time killer with a unique aesthetic that has an extremely fair price point. 
 
If you ARE looking at this game and consider yourself completionist, just steer clear. The corpse and memory card system is so fundamentally disrespectful to the players time that I can't wrap my head around it. Locking the games core replayability/reward structure around its own innate hard-layered RNG-dependent gameplay and various other forms of soft RNG is cartoonish. Seriously, imagine if you couldn't fight Mega Satan or Hush in The Binding of Isaac because your PREVIOUS run wasn't good enough- or worse yet, because your run was incredible, you were only given the option to go fight other bosses that you've already beaten.  
 
If I have to give CloverPit anything, it's that it successfully Ludonarrative Dissonance'd me away from the gambling addiction it's trying to provide through horrible game design, so good job!

It's fun but the percentages are just a smokescreen.. You can have nothing increasing the base chance of getting 666 but have 3 items for the 7 and yet every other to every run you still get 666..  0.6-1.5% my ass.

This game gets harder every game you play. Not because of intended difficulty spikes, but because the meta progression makes it more difficult to get the needed trinkets (buyable upgrades) that you need to pass the level. For example trinkets that wont trigger for 2 deadlines away (any 666 trigger trinkets) 6 rounds of not useful and a waste of space. I get that it is a luck based game. 
The game also doesn't respect your time. The animations get tedious. 
 
Every time you end a round (3 rounds in every deadline) it is 3 animations that are 2 seconds long and you might think that isn't all that much, but it adds up. Waiting for the slot machine is one thing, but to wait on unskippable animations just to tell you what you already know gets old and feels condescending. After some point the animation needs to 1 speed up, be removed, or an optional opt out. 
 
idk, It is a good "numbers go up" game, but it feels like an exercise in Sisyphus as you reset. Bad seed, bad luck, redo, it becomes frustrating at some point and you have to ask yourself is this worth my time?

After giving a good faith try on this patch, I am having a really hard time understanding how any of this makes the game better or is pro-engagement. Forcing you to beat Hardmode on every card rather than having a choice, screws everyone that didn't grind the game before. It should be a choice. 
 
Nerfing the endgame to stop you from going infinite makes 0 sense, there is no correlation between endgame content and having an infinite run. 
 
SPOILERS: Literally using Holy Phone usually nerfs your run from taking advantage of red phone calls and forcing 7's to 84% and having their base value in the e's. 
 
Seems like the devs don't have an understanding of what is actually powerful vs what they nerfed. Nerfing cigarettes because you can use it to restock a bunch of times seemed like it's main purpose, it restocks your shop - 1 slot, upgrading things by base value past deadline 3 is not viable and a waste of time honestly, you should be atleast multiplying it or working on something else. 
 
BTW I am an all achievements room 11 player currently. I love the ♥♥♥♥ out of this game, but this patch is so bad except for hourglass and bell rework those can stay.

The devs have made the choice to nerf items in a SINGLE PLAYER GAME. They no longer allow high tier/infinite runs because why? Who knows. They managed to kill the only end game goal and essentially ruin the replayability of the game. It was a great game, it is now......uninstalled.

Game is a blast, but also unstable, and designed to penalize you if you crash to prevent cheaters/save scumming. I don't care if other people want to cheat, and its now happened to me multiple times on the Steam Machine (which it is verified for). Also, the better a run is going, the more unstable the client becomes. Horrible design choice.
had a really lucky first run but unlocked so many mediocre charms that its basically impossible to beat that without hours of boring restarts.

It's fun when you get a good run, but having to constantly reset because the very first deadline is LITERALLY UNCLEARABLE on so many seeds is just bad game design, especially considering the memory card modifiers are consumed on run start. Want to do a specific modified run? Better hope you get a good seed, because there's maybe a 50/50 shot that you get to even play the game.

Love the game, but its very unstable on linux (CachyOS and SteamDeck both). 
 
I am getting memory leaks. I'll change the review until its fixed.

Early on, the game is very fun. With wins and losses, you begin to plan for winning strategies and combos with your charms. 

For context: Charms act as purchasable modifiers for a run. You have a initial 5 randomly picked at that start of your run and they are re-rolled at the start of every new deadline or "level". You have the ability to spend money to restock/re-roll the available charms and the cost scales with every cleared level or purchase.

As you progress through deadlines "levels", you unlock additional charms added to the pool for future strategies and combos.

You continue to unlock more charms! And... more charms..... and even more and more charms. 

Your early progression slows, you find it harder and harder to progress with a planned strat to due the rng of the charm pool.

After a certain point you have rearched "Charm Bloat"

Your spending less time playing the game and more time hitting "restart" at the start of a run because the rng of your initial charm selection gives you no path forward. Occasionally the stars will align and you will get a decent run only to be rewarded with.... you guess it! More Charms.

So is the game worth the asking price? Yes and no. 
Does it provide hours of funs early on? Yes and that may be worth your money.

However if you looking for one of those roguelikes that you will come back to and sink hours in it again every few months, this is not it. In it current state it punishes you the more you play it and the charm system needS

Was really fun up to the point where you opened the fourth drawer - ever since, the game becomes pretty much unplayable - I know it's supposed to be luck based but in all honesty I've tried for several days now again and again, different strategies, different charms - its just not even fun anymore at this point and that sucks. It just feels like an actual slot machine now, you lose every time no matter what you try.

Game is great and really fun and has awesome mechanics and very addictive gameplay. HOWEVER, the further you get in playing the more charms you unlock which becomes a PROBLEM for one simple reason: so many of the charms the devs made are pure, unfettered ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Now, if you could ban some of these charms or make sure they never showed up in the pool again, you could negate this. As it stands, you lose about 8/10 runs due to sorting through all the waste to try and find something that syngerizes with your various other charms and telephone abilities.  
 
Its a shame, because the game is just so interesting and I keep wanting to come back for more, but then I do come back and just get bogged down with how horrible the RNG is, and when I see the stupid ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ depression charm for the millionth time I just sigh now.  
 
Also, the challenge runs being consumable cards is a cool idea in theory, but with how awful it is to get a run going off the ground, it just de-incentivizes me to waste these consumables knowing the odds are heavily weighed against the run even seeing the fourth deadline.  
 
All in all, the game has such fantastic promise and is genuinely fun in the beginning before you start diluting your charm pool with the complete surplus of dog-water charms. If the devs implement a system to counteract this fundamental design flaw, I wouldn't be able to put the game down. I got instantly hooked on this game when a friend introduced it to me, to the point it's the first game I ever tried to 100% purely out of enjoyment. However, the recent update has lead to nothing but disappointment.

CloverPot's new item description is confusing. There are also typos in the description of some items. A very sloppy update from my perspective. The recent nerfs took out a lot of things without enough buffs or changes to supplement for what was lost. Endless run strats may feel cheap, but those were only viable because building with other items that are very underwhelming is not enjoyable either. Besides, these endless runs are optional -- if the player finds it cheap or not fun to play, they don't HAVE to try these strategies.

Also ever since 1.2 dropped, I have noticed the CPU usage of CloverPit randomly jumps between 3% - 20% on my device. After having the game open for a while, the game is completely laggy and I go from 120 frames per second to 30 frames per chance.

Instead of nerfing/buffing items, perhaps consider adding Quality of Life changes to the game. There are several things that I feel require more attention than knocking out endless run strats which aren't even required to beat the game. I propose the following QoL:
- hotswapping items in drawers,
- automatic unpacking of memory cards,
- auto-decline deals,
- accessibility settings to reduce the amount of flashy animations in the game (the game becomes an eyesore at one point just because it bli

Honestly one of the worst ways to throw away your money on a luck trap. Small spoiler, you have cards in the game that alter the gameplay. These cards either give a buff, or a change and because of the change a nerf with for example, getting an empty charm shop after finishing a deadline in exchange for phone buffs being double value. But here is the problem, you need luck to win the first round. It looks fun to try and finish the game with most cards, and especially on hardmode. But here is the catch, you often enough wont get past round one. Crazy right? You spend one of these cards, and lose it before you can make good use of it. Like the double phone buff, if you dont make the deadline you never get called and you never used the card while losing. This is a huge issue, it is not fun to keep on grinding and hope you get lucky. It completely ruins the game, there should at least be some mechanism to make sure you often enough survive round one. Like why would I ever try holographic cards, where your debt is double, if I can't even get the normal debt amount all of the time?

From the experience I had, this means you'll need to stack up at least 10 cards of the one you want to do, then hope some of them get into the second deadline so you have a chance to actually beat the game. And this all also depends on which charms you get, its all fun and games getting 3 and 4 ticket charms in your shop when you have only 2 tickets. I know it might look odd - "92hrs played at the time of review, and it's not recommended?". Trust me, I really really want to love this game, and theres many parts of it I do love! Still though, I cant recommend it to others. Maybe I'm being overly critical, but it feels too... plain? I was drawn to Clover Pit because of my love for ficitional gambling, crunchy graphics, and macabre themes. I love the aesthetic, the sound design, the graphics, etc. Beautiful. 11/10. The gameplay loop is simple enough and easy to understand, and the universe you're placed in gives you just enough to want to learn Why You're There.  
The game gets really tiring really fast, though. I unlocked all the charms and started theorizing what different builds there could be, and theres really only the same few builds... I know, I know - that's kinda how all roguelikes are; "Get these same 6 items and you automatically win the game ggez, go next", but I genuinely didnt feel the need to use the majority of the charms available, and I'd be surprised if you actually could? It felt simultaneously IMPOSSIBLY difficult and INCREDIBLY easy. It all just felt tedious. Either you dont spin enough to get past the first round or you immediately get all the charms you need and you fly through. the majority of the memory card challenges I didnt even have to worry about the challenge rules - I got my Ticket Build, scored 1mil coins, and skipped the last 4 rounds. Having bought the game in 1.1 and now having lost four matches in a row before the third deadline in 1.2, scoring a grand total of 56 coins on my last third deadline, I'll just say this: whatever the devs did to version 1.2, they should change it back. As it stands right now, this otherwise really fun game wastes my time and that's sad. Uninstalled.
This game has a big crashing problem on steam deck I tried to fix it but nothing works so devs please fix it

Over the few runs I did, no matter how good my "build" was, I never really felt like I had an influence in the game like other roguelikes. I just pull a lever and watch everything else happen, hoping enough stars will align so I can get to the next quota. I dunno, maybe that's the whole point, but it doesn't really make for good gameplay in my eyes.
I'm sure others enjoy it, but I didn't.

Until the hard mode patch gets reverted, don't buy this game, they managed to steal my money, don't let them steal yours.

Edit: Word is they are working on a hotfix. Until I see proper tangible fixes here, I'm not about to change this review. 1.2 shows they haven't thought their changes through, and whatever this hotfix is might follow that pattern. If you have bought this game and can't refund, check the discussions, one of them will tell you how to revert these changes for your copy, for better or worse, up to you though.

1.3 Edit: And so they followed that pattern, so I'll do two things, leave this review up, and never touch this game again. It's crystal clear they never have and never will understand what made people flock to it. The attitude expressed over on their instagram has continued grow with in the patches (https://www.instagram.com/reel/DRAPaLakwpW/?utm_source=ig_web_copy_link). Meanwhile the descussions about this game almost always grind to a halt by people who decry skill issues without understanding the rng required in many cases. Simply put, I'm done, either save your money or demand better from panik arcade, but I can't anymore.

Why do I have to do a failed run in order to unlock the possibility to win a run? Why are the fun challenges consumable? Why are they not only consumable, but require you to have a very strong run already, then deliberately handicap yourself to get a *chance* at new, fun ideas? Why does this game make me waste my time in order to get to the bits that are interesting and fun?

It was fun for some time, but then it gets too repetitive.
Most charms and phone selections are useless, so good strategies are not very different from each other.

There were just few updates which have not delivered anything really fun, but instead nerfed all funny strategies.
Then there were no updates for 3+ months, but now they release a paid DLC 🤡

Prefer supporting less greedy and lazy devs

Prevent you from getting past the first round?

Not a single worthwhile QoL improvement

A lot of the random seeds for runs make it impossible to get past the first two rounds, to the point that the player's decisions actually don't matter. I'm not sure if this was a development oversight, lack of testing, or something I'm missing, but realizing a large number of the runs were doomed from the start, regardless of my decisions, ruined the fun of this game. While this is great for expressing the despairs of gambling addiction, I don't really want to waste my time plugging through doomed seeds to explore the full game, whenever I hit the right random seeds. It makes the rogue-like part of the game feel so small.

This is a game that is less interested with game design in mind and more so based on the design of actual gambling. So it preys on that "one more hit" part of your brain, but not so much the positive feedback loop that comes with classic game design. As a result, I personally felt very bad (sometimes actually sick) after playing since it does not really respect your time if your particularly unlucky- which you will be for the first 10 hours or so. 
 
That said, while predatory, it is a well-made game. So I'm more so making this review for the odd person who has had gambling addiction to please stay away. A gambling-prone personality WILL be caught by this games grip, and there is no payoff at the end.

After update this game went down the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Even with normal memory card selected and normal difficulty the RNG in after the update seems ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ terrible. Spent 3 hours spinning and working previous builds and cannot even make it past the 2222 coin deadline. Do not recommend this anymore especially since before the big update this game was a blast.

This game reminds me why I hate real-life gambling. I've always been unlucky with dice rolling, slots, even cards, but this  game really emphasizes that if you have bad luck in general, you're just going to have a bad time. No real meta progression, every run is as new as the last except for a few more "charms" added to your pool that you need less spins to have enough tickets to afford and then you just lose every spin, get no coins and die anyway.

I thought I'd give it a shot because I had a lot of fun with Scritchy Scratchy, but no - just not for me. I don't think it's inherently a 'bad game' but due to the lack of meaningful progression mechanics, I think the popularly defined user tag of 'roguelite' is extremely generous and is more aligned to the other tag of being a 'roguelike' with how extremely punishing it is with loop ends with the added bonus of a painfully forward hostile RNG center-focus which is why I'm rating it negatively. I mean... 2 666's in a row early game with 'just' a 1.5% chance? Nah, that's when I pulled the plug on this adventure.

I really like the concept..... but it feels like this game punishes you the more you play it. As you continue to unlock different charms, it becomes more and more difficult to build any sort of synergy. I'm a big fan of roguelike/lites and they are one of my most commonly played genres, so I'm no stranger to losing.... a lot... and this feels different to me. I guess it is gambling, so it stands to reason that it just feels like pure RNG, but it's not as fun when it feels like it's impossible to actually use skill or strategy to win. It's bordering on brainrot as a result. Still better than real gambling!

The game isn't bad, it's slop but thats kind of a given and the game doesn't really pretend to not be, my main gripe is once you start getting some unlocks the game just becomes a restart simulator.

Since the initial deadline is so tight you basically need to have a playable build right from the start so basically every run is start>check the trinket shop > continue or reset (90% of the times its reset), this isn't the only roguelike where this is a problem but in most other games you have a level of mechanical skill associated with the gameplay so you can make up for poor starts with good gameplay, here it's a literal slot machine, you can get a good start but bad rolls and you lose, you can get a mediocre start with bad rolls and lose or you can get a bad start and instatly get a 7 Jackpot and automatically beat the 1st deadline.

I know you might think "oh wow the slot machine game has random chance, what did you expect dumbass" but there is only so many times you can see your build crumble because you got dealt a bad roll by a random number generator before you start thinking you could be playing something else thats actually more fun.

I would have recommended this if you liked games like Balatro where seeing the big number go up and manipulating RNG through careful inventory management, but as of the most recent update the developers seem oddly hell-bent on PREVENTING endless runs for no reason, even though they are incredibly hard to actually pull off and can lead to a lot of failures.

It is weird in general for a developer to nerf elements of a single player game THIS hard? Just look up the patch 1.2 notes and see for yourself if you care about the fine details, but basically they made the game harder, they nerfed the ability to do endless runs, and they rebalanced a lot of things for the worse.

The game itself is a good metaphor for the shallow and vapid nature of gambling wins. You play as an unspecified damned soul in a hell-like cage where after a while, even a Jackpot means nothing as it isn't enough, it's never enough. Ultimately the way to "win" and escape is by rejecting the call of gaming more and more away and to just let go.
Good game all together, decent content and is still fun after playing awhile. The DLC they just released "Unholy Fusion" should be free, the DLC barely has any content and it's not even worth the $3.

After almost two months, the game got a big update making some of the achievements basically impossible without an unreasonable amount of grinding for tens of hours just to try and get them. In its current state, the game is no fun anymore.
Game was fun until devs nerfed everything in a patch.  Now you can't win, and the game I bought and enjoyed no longer exists.  Buyer beware.

This game needs a "toggler" feature like megabonk. There's waaay more trash items here. It was fun at the start, actually winning 3 straight games back to back (unlocking the key). But after you unlock enough items, the item pool gets diluted with garbage effects and it starts to feel bad. 

Too many runs die with no fault of your own. At least balatro feels it's possible to beat all seeds to be beatable until purple stakes and up. It's amazing to think about how balanced balatro's joker cards with the sheer amount of cards there and it doesn't need to have a toggler to do it.
